array-clear-range.title: Reset part of an array with Array.Clear
array-clear-range.short: Clear a range back to default values
array-clear-range.summary: Array.Clear resets elements in a specified range to their type's default value, avoiding a hand-written clearing loop.
array-clear-range.why: It keeps range handling concise when only part of a reusable array needs to be reset.
array-clear-range.tips: Reference elements become null, numeric elements become zero, and other values become default(T).

bitoperations-popcount.title: Count set bits with BitOperations.PopCount
bitoperations-popcount.summary: BitOperations.PopCount returns the number of one bits in an integer and is useful for flags and compact bit sets.
bitoperations-popcount.why: It states the operation directly and lets the runtime use optimized instructions when available.
bitoperations-popcount.tips: Unsigned integer types usually make the intended bit representation easiest to reason about.

enumerable-distinctby.title: Remove duplicates by key with DistinctBy
enumerable-distinctby.short: Keep one element for each selected key
enumerable-distinctby.summary: DistinctBy keeps the first element encountered for each distinct selected key, making ID-based deduplication concise.
enumerable-distinctby.why: It expresses the intent more directly than GroupBy followed by selecting one element from each group.
enumerable-distinctby.tips: Which element survives depends on enumeration order, so sort first when the choice matters.

enumerable-maxby.title: Select the element with the largest key using MaxBy
enumerable-maxby.short: Get the source element, not just its maximum value
enumerable-maxby.summary: MaxBy returns the source element whose selected key is greatest, such as the most expensive product.
enumerable-maxby.why: It avoids computing Max and then enumerating again to locate the matching element.
enumerable-maxby.tips: Check the empty-sequence behavior for your element type and make the input contract explicit.

file-readlines-streaming.title: Stream large text files with File.ReadLines
file-readlines-streaming.short: Process lines without loading the whole file
file-readlines-streaming.summary: File.ReadLines lazily enumerates lines, allowing large text files to be processed one line at a time.
file-readlines-streaming.why: Unlike ReadAllLines, it does not require an array containing the entire file, reducing peak memory use.
file-readlines-streaming.tips: The file remains involved while enumeration is active, so process needed data during the enumeration.

json-polymorphism-attributes.title: Configure derived JSON types with attributes
json-polymorphism-attributes.short: Declare discriminators and allowed derived types
json-polymorphism-attributes.summary: JsonPolymorphic and JsonDerivedType let System.Text.Json serialize known derived types through a base-type property.
json-polymorphism-attributes.why: The accepted derived types and their discriminators stay explicit in code instead of relying on ambiguous type restoration.
json-polymorphism-attributes.tips: For external input, register only the derived types you actually intend to accept.

memory-stream-getbuffer.title: Avoid a copy with MemoryStream.TryGetBuffer
memory-stream-getbuffer.short: Access an exposable internal buffer safely
memory-stream-getbuffer.summary: TryGetBuffer obtains an ArraySegment<byte> over an exposable MemoryStream buffer without copying all bytes.
memory-stream-getbuffer.why: It can avoid the full allocation and copy performed by ToArray for large in-memory payloads.
memory-stream-getbuffer.tips: Not every MemoryStream exposes its buffer; always handle the false result.

string-contains-comparison.title: Specify StringComparison with Contains
string-contains-comparison.summary: The StringComparison overload of string.Contains lets code state case and culture rules directly at the search site.
string-contains-comparison.why: It avoids temporary strings from ToLower-style approaches and documents the intended comparison semantics.
string-contains-comparison.tips: Prefer Ordinal variants for identifiers and protocol values; consider culture-aware comparison for human text.

task-whenany-timeout.title: Build custom timeouts with Task.WhenAny
task-whenany-timeout.short: Race an operation against a delay
task-whenany-timeout.summary: Task.WhenAny can race an operation against a delay when timeout handling needs more control than a simple wait.
task-whenany-timeout.why: It supports custom logging, fallback work, or other behavior when the timeout task wins.
task-whenany-timeout.tips: A timeout does not automatically stop the original Task; design cancellation separately when the operation must stop.

weakreference-cache.title: Keep reclaimable references with WeakReference<T>
weakreference-cache.short: Reference an object without keeping it alive
weakreference-cache.summary: WeakReference<T> does not strongly root its target, allowing the GC to collect the object when no strong references remain.
weakreference-cache.why: It can support opportunistic reuse of expensive but recreatable objects while they happen to remain alive.
weakreference-cache.tips: Treat the target as optional at every access and handle TryGetTarget returning false.
